fields.value: One experiment-file model, one launch pass, and a machine launcher beneath it

An experiment file declares its work with fixed names — `training_jobs()`, `eval_jobs(state)`, `report()` — and each declaration returns every job that should have been run, or can be run, by now. `etude train` and `etude eval` do the work on this machine; `etude launch` and `etude queue` get machines for both stages and run what has not been run.

Launching has two levels. A machine launcher puts a run on a machine with the job's and the machine's own limits and knows nothing of experiments. An experiment launcher above it reads the file, observes state, calls the declarations, hands down the runs that are new and owns the experiment's limits. Nothing sits between them: cohorts are removed.

Today the training declaration is read as `runs`, the eval declaration as `eval(state)`, jobs are built by `training(...)` / `evaluation(...)`, `etude launch` reads only the training declaration, `etude eval` both plays here and rents machines, and limits that span runs live on named cohorts inside the scheduler.

Outcome: the renames (old names refused, no aliases); `TrainingJob` and `EvalJob` as subclasses of `Job`, each declaration returning only its kind, names required; `training_jobs` may take `state`, and state includes eval runs; one launch pass for both stages keyed by run address and keeping no private memory; `etude eval` only plays here; the two launch levels with a layout rule a test enforces; limits on jobs, machines and the experiment only. Job identity and stored runs stay readable; the launcher database version changes. Upgrade note in `release/UNRELEASED.md`; no version change and no release. Manabot pins the merged commit (MTG-329).

The accepted design is `scratch/design.md` in the Task checkout; the discussion and Jack Heart's words are in `scratch/sdk-hierarchy.md`. PR #113 is updated in place. Command-line config overrides are EXP-67.
